reasons: Direction is correct: Section 6.1 binds the Company (our client, the customer receiving development/hosting services) not to participate in competing Internet projects for the full rolling term, with no performance exit — squarely the EXCLUSIVITY walk-away position, so a deviation finding is warranted.

The redline lands on the stated fallback: it confines the restriction to the defined 'Deerskin Products' category (dropping the sweeping 'products substantially similar ... Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled' extension), caps it at twelve months instead of the auto-renewing term, and adds automatic termination on HDI's failure to meet service levels, availability requirements or delivery dates (including the Section 1.6 launch date).

Customer-favourable elements are preserved as the rule requires: Section 6.2 closeout carve-out and HDI's reciprocal covenant in Section 6.3 are untouched, and HDI's brand exclusivity is made to fall away on the same triggers rather than surviving.

The failed 'minimal edit' checks are advisory only here — converting a full-term, broad-category exclusive into a 12-month, category-limited, performance-terminable covenant necessarily requires rewriting the clause, and the surviving text tracks the original wording closely.
The comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, cites the playbook position and the fallback offered, and correctly states that Section 6.3 is unchanged.

Minor drafting nit to tighten on the next pass: 'the Effective Date' is not a defined term in this Agreement (which is 'dated as of August 9, 1999'); consider 'the date of this Agreement' or 'the launch date under Section 1.6' to avoid ambiguity about when the twelve-month period starts.
